### According to Flora of Somalia

M. Thulin et al. Flora of Somalia, Vol. 1-4 [updated 2008] https://plants.jstor.org/collection/FLOS

Morphology General Habit
    Annual herb, 0.1–0.8 m tall; stems moderately to densely pubescent with recurved hairs
Morphology Leaves
    Leaves petiolate or upper leaves sessile; blade ovate to lanceolate, up to 20–110 × 12–45 mm, 1.8–3 times as long as wide, apex subacute, acute or slightly acuminate, margin crenate-serrate
Morphology Reproductive morphology Inflorescences
    Verticillasters ± spaced, globose; cymes many-flowered; bracteoles 6–10 mm long; pedicels 0–0.5 mm long
Morphology Reproductive morphology Fruits Fruiting calyx
    Fruiting calyx 10-lobed, strongly zygomorphic, 10–12 mm long at the dorsal side, 9–11 mm long at the ventral side; tube slightly upcurved at the middle and strongly recurved near the mouth; upper lobe 3–4 mm long, other lobes much shorter
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Corolla
    Corolla 5–7 mm long; lower lip ± as long as upper lip
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Gynoecium Style
    Style-branches very unequal
Morphology Reproductive morphology Fruits
    Nutlets 1.4–1.8 × 0.8–1 mm, smooth and glossy, apex rounded and with sessile glands.
Distribution
    N1, 2 widespread in tropical and southern Africa, also introduced in other parts of the tropics.
Ecology
    Altitude range 650–1580 m.
[FSOM]

Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Androecium Stamens Filaments
    Filaments with eglandular hairs about halfway up
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Gynoecium Stigma
    Stigma unequally lobed
Morphology Reproductive morphology Fruits
    Nutlets 1.5–2 mm long, with some glands
Ecology
    Widespread weed on cultivated land and in gardens; 0–1800 m
Conservation
    Least concern; widely distributed
Note
    Extremely widespread but surprisingly consistent in morphology (at least within the area of the Flora of Tropical East Africa and Flora Zambesiaca), although there is some variation in the leaf shape and indumentum. Leucas martinicensis is distinctive because of its globose verticils, somewhat sigmoid calyx with conspicuous central posterior calyx lobe, and tiny corolla (4–6 mm long) within which the typical band of glandular hairs is absent.
Distribution
    Range: Widespread throughout Africa, also in Madagascar and the Yemen and introduced to the neotropics Flora districts: U1 U2 U3 U4 K1 K3 K4 K5 K6 K7T1 T2 T3 T4 T5 T6 T7 T8 Z
[FTEA]

    Calyx tube somewhat ventrally gibbous, dorsal side curving over conspicuously at mouth as fruit matures, ± sigmoid in appearance, 7–8 mm long at anthesis, extending 2–3 mm in fruit, pubescent with long hairs on vein ridges, hairs shorter in between, with yellow sessile glands, inner surface with short appressed hairs; throat ± symmetric; lobes 10, all narrowly triangular to subulate with spinescent tips, centre lobes on posterior side longer, 2–4 mm, sometimes almost erect, conspicuous, other lobes 1–2 mm long, subequal-Corolla white with darker coloration on anterior lip, 4–6 mm long; tube 3.5–4 mm long with appressed hairs in upper half, band of glandular hairs absent on tube inner surface; posterior lip 1.5–2 mm long, anterior lip 2–3 mm long, inner surface with small papillae, outer surface with scattered hairs
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Androecium Stamens Filaments
    Filaments with eglandular hairs about halfway up
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Gynoecium Stigma
    Stigma unequally lobed
Morphology Reproductive morphology Fruits
    Nutlets 1.5–2 mm long, with some glands.
Distribution
    Zambia, Zimbabwe, Malawi, Mozambique. Widespread throughout Africa, also in Madagascar and Yemen; introduced to the neotropics.
Ecology
    Widespread weed on cultivated land and in gardens; 100–1400 m.
Conservation
    Widespread; Least Concern.
Recognition
    Extremely widespread but surprisingly consistent in morphology (at least within the F.T.E.A. and Flora Zambesiaca areas), although there is some variation in the leaf shape and indumentum. Leucas martinicensis is distinctive because of its globose verticils, somewhat sigmoid calyx with conspicuous central posterior calyx lobe, and tiny corolla (4–6 mm long), within which the typical band of glandular hairs is absent.
